issues.title: Reconcile Ciani2026 effluent biosorption pretreatment, units and replicate handling
issues.body:
Primary: Ciani et al. (2026), *Toward Industrial Application of Cyanobacterial Biosorption: Insights From Real Electroplating Effluents*, [DOI 10.1002/wer.70366](https://doi.org/10.1002/wer.70366), PMCID PMC13037690. Complete original seven-page PDF, XML, Figures 1–4 and original DOCX Tables S1–S4 are acquired. This is a source clarification follow-up, not a request to close a demonstrated defect in the qualified electroplating-bath-effluents record.

The acquired source has unresolved discrepancies:

- Section 3.1 assigns HCl-pretreated biosorbents to the Ni(1)+Cu/Ni(2) arms; section 3.2 later describes the Ni/Cu treatment as alkaline. The cited Ciani2024 protocol specifies acid pretreatment but does not establish the 2026 NaOH duration/wash sequence.
- Original PDF Figures 3–4 use micromol/g DW in axes and captions. PMC XML/HTML captions use mmol/g DW. These differ by a factor of 1000 and must remain version-specific.
- Table S3 gives 16Som2 Pd uptake 8.14, 8.09 and 0.00 mg/g DW. All three values do not reproduce the main-text 76.2±0.3 micromol/g summary. The zero row must not be silently excluded. Table S1 CE4 and Table S3 Vi22M each include a missing row despite nominal triplicates.
- Section 3.2 says Cu/Zn uptake was always below 20 micromol/g DW, but S1 CE4 Cu 2.25 mg/g and S2 16Som2 Zn 1.72 mg/g exceed that threshold on the stated molar basis.

Acceptance requires an attributable primary clarification, corrected version or underlying assay data identifying each pretreatment arm, original control/treatment concentrations and biomass masses, handling of missing/zero rows, unit correction and exact replicate statistics. Preserve the current originals and compare revised bytes and formulas. Do not infer whole-feed recovery, culture viability, a molecular binding cause or industrial operation from the existing specific-uptake assay. Do not contact authors automatically.

The initial paginated all-state issue inventory (270 items) was searched for the DOI, Ciani, Galvanica and cyanobacterial-biosorption wording; no source-specific duplicate was identified. Existing #178 concerns Kordloo electroplating sludge and remains separate. A refreshed paginated all-state inventory of 177 non-PR issues on 2026-10-14 also contained no matching DOI or source-specific issue.

Raw provenance: `/private/tmp/cmm-round82-resources-research/`. Accepted PDF SHA256 `223ba8896a7a60f922f6065f76aa073e0f4130cad70d75ddda5cf759a7852f99`; original DOCX SHA256 `b515b26d7184f2346d0425c9deca686d7dd043b454c66d00956e860a9ce08ec4`.

issues.title: Acquire complete Chang 2021 tiemannite methylation primary and official supplement
issues.body:
Chang Q., Zhang Z., Ji Y., Tian L., Chen W. and Zhang T. (2021), *Natural organic matter facilitates formation and microbial methylation of mercury selenide nanoparticles*, Environmental Science: Nano 8, 67–75. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/D0EN00992J.

This is a promising new HgSe mineral owner: indexed primary text assigns abiotic NOM-associated precipitates to tiemannite by HRTEM/XRD, then tests bacterial methylation. It must remain separate from metacinnabar (HgS), generic mercury–selenium associations and microbial mineral formation. ND132 is now mapped by NCBI to Pseudodesulfovibrio mercurii (641491), while the paper uses Desulfovibrio desulfuricans ND132.

The round82 acquisition attempt on 2026-10-14 obtained Crossref metadata and mineral/taxon authorities, but not a complete locally inspectable original main or supplement. The publisher main HTML and landing page returned HTTP403; the indexed official SI URL https://www.rsc.org/suppdata/d0/en/d0en00992j/d0en00992j1.pdf returned404 both through direct acquisition and web opening. Search indexing exposes primary text and the SI title, which does not establish present full-document or figure access. ResearchGate explicitly offered a request, not full text. No authentication, challenge bypass, author contact or repeated unchanged retry was used. No tiemannite record was created.

Acceptance for a later curation:

- Obtain a legitimate complete main original or accepted manuscript and the full official SI; retain exact acquisition routes, versions, file types, dates and hashes.
- Inspect all main figures, phase-defining HRTEM/XRD (reported S1–S3), methylation controls, full synthesis/aging and incubation methods, NOM composition and source/denominator definitions. Verify whether unprecipitated Hg or NOM carryover confounds the mineral-specific comparison.
- Preserve the distinction between chemical HgSe precipitation and subsequent microbial transformation, the organism's historical/current name, particle size/aging limits, abiotic/bulk controls and laboratory scale. Do not infer product recovery or inherited criticality.
- Search source corrections and directly relevant counterevidence; review a prospective owner independently before acceptance.

Evidence and exact failures are retained externally under /private/tmp/cmm-round82-sulfides-research (acquisition-authorized.json, crossref-tiemannite.json and query-log.json). Initial round82 all-state issue inventory and hidden/ignored-inclusive maintained/root-bound raw searches showed no matching DOI/mineral acquisition issue; the refreshed all-state inventory of 177 non-PR issues on 2026-10-14 likewise contained no matching DOI or source-specific issue.
